fields.sample_size: documentary analysis of the Brazilian legal and institutional framework plus a review of ANA data on sewage treatment plants in operation nationally (UASB reactors and septic tanks with anaerobic filters most used)
fields.effect_estimate: The most used decentralised technologies (UASB reactors; septic tank plus anaerobic filter) lack federal regulation defining who is responsible for managing them; only two states have rules assigning that responsibility and only three states (Southeast and South) have laws on septic-tank-plus-filter systems where there is no public collection network; effort is needed to extend services, especially in rural, peri-urban and hard-to-reach areas. Documentary and descriptive; no effect estimates.
fields.study_design: jurimetric documentary analysis of legal and institutional framework with national treatment-plant data
fields.section: Full text: Methodology; Results (technologies from ANA data; legal framework by level); Discussion
fields.exact_location: Methodology; Results (technologies from ANA data; legal framework by level); Discussion

evidence_level: Single-study evidence: a documentary analysis of the Brazilian legal framework for decentralised sewage management with ANA treatment-plant data, read in full text 2026-10-04. No federal rule assigns responsibility for the commonest decentralised systems; two states assign it and three regulate septic-tank-plus-filter systems. Descriptive.
pdf_note: Revista de Gestao Ambiental e Sustentabilidade / engineering journal (2021), about 70,000 characters read
notes: Abstract-level extraction accurate; adds the ANA data basis. Direct evidence for the 'unclear responsibility / gap in regulation' mechanism.
